extracted.intended_audience: recipients of federal education funding (K-12 and postsecondary institutions), Title IX coordinators, institutional administrators, legal counsel, and policy practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for identifying, evaluating, and enforcing hostile environment sex-based harassment under Title IX in the administrative (federal enforcement) context, including interactions with First Amendment concerns and required institutional grievance procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hostile environment sex-based harassment — required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: To establish hostile environment sex-based harassment the conduct must be: (1) unwelcome, (2) sex-based, (3) subjectively and objectively offensive, and (4) so severe or pervasive (5) that it results in a limitation or denial of a person's ability to participate in or benefit from the recipient's education program or activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The final definition adds the word “offensive” to the subjective/objective prong. The Department requires satisfaction of all listed elements before a hostile environment is established. The definition is intended to effectuate Title IX's nondiscrimination mandate in the administrative enforcement context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Totality of circumstances / individualized determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether unwelcome sex-based conduct has created a hostile environment is determined based on the totality of the circumstances and requires an individualized determination.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recipients must consider surrounding circumstances including the ages, roles, and other relevant characteristics of the parties (e.g., student vs employee). The same conduct may be permissible between employees yet prohibited between students or between a student and an employee. Evaluations must be context-specific.

rubrics_metrics.name: Severe or pervasive (administrative standard) vs Davis standard
rubrics_metrics.description: For administrative enforcement the final regulations require that conduct be subjectively and objectively offensive and be either severe or pervasive, rather than the Davis private-damages phrasing of “severe, pervasive, and objectively offensive.”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department explains the administrative standard is broader because the goal is to ensure access to education (not to set the high bar appropriate for private monetary damages). A single serious incident may be sufficiently severe to create a hostile environment; pervasive conduct may create a hostile environment even if no single incident is severe. This difference is lawful and tied to the distinct purposes of administrative enforcement vs private litigation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of First Amendment limits
rubrics_metrics.description: Nothing in the Title IX regulations requires a recipient to restrict rights protected by the First Amendment (see §106.6(d)). Recipients must formulate, interpret, and apply rules in a manner that respects constitutional rights.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department affirms commitment to freedom of speech, academic freedom, religious liberty, and freedom of association. In applying the hostile-environment definition, recipients should avoid actions that would unlawfully restrict protected speech; recipients have other means to remedy hostile environments consistent with the First Amendment. The preamble addresses concerns about compelled speech, content- and viewpoint-based regulation, and potential chilling effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grievance procedure protections to ensure fair process
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients are required to adopt grievance procedures that include procedural protections to effectuate investigations and evidence-based determinations designed to ensure a fair process for all parties.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Required protections include, for example, equitable treatment of parties, an equal opportunity to access relevant evidence, and the objective evaluation of all relevant and not otherwise impermissible evidence prior to a determination. See §§106.45 and 106.46 for detailed procedural requirements. These protections help prevent unfair discipline and protect respondents' rights.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative enforcement process and corrective measures
rubrics_metrics.description: In administrative enforcement, a recipient must be given notice and an opportunity to come into compliance before termination of funding (20 U.S.C. 1682); investigations typically lead to agreements to take corrective measures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department relies on notice-and-corrective-measure guardrails in justifying a lower administrative bar than for private damages. Administrative remedies differ from private monetary remedies and inform the appropriate regulatory standard and response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alignment with Title VII while tailoring for educational settings
rubrics_metrics.description: The final definition aligns closely with Title VII hostile-environment sexual harassment definitions but is expressly tailored for education programs and activities under Title IX.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Alignment offers administrative and compliance benefits for many recipients who must comply with both Title IX and Title VII; nevertheless, the Department crafted the Title IX definition to reflect differences between workplace and educational environments.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoiding overbroad reporting, tracking, and investigation practices that chill speech
rubrics_metrics.description: Policymaking and institutional procedures should avoid creating reporting or investigatory regimes that in practice chill classroom discussion, academic inquiry, or protected speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters raised concerns that broad reporting requirements could bring nearly all sex-related classroom discussions under investigation. The Department responds that the final definition and §106.6(d) protect speech, but institutions should be mindful in implementing reporting/tracking policies so as not to unduly chill academic freedom or lawful expression.

rubrics_metrics.name: Respect for academic freedom, religious liberty, and freedom of association
rubrics_metrics.description: Application of the hostile-environment definition and grievance procedures must respect academic freedom, religious liberty, and freedom of association rights of students, faculty, and institutions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Department notes concerns that regulations might force suppression of religiously informed views or compel associations to include members contrary to their viewpoints. The regulations do not require recipients to punish religious exercise or to endorse/suppress views in ways that violate sincerely held beliefs; institutions should interpret and apply policies consistent with constitutional protections.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate differentiation between administrative enforcement standards and private-damages standards
rubrics_metrics.description: The Department may adopt a standard for administrative enforcement that differs from the standard courts use to assess private damages liability (Davis/Gebser framework).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Davis and Gebser addressed the context of private monetary damages and the burdens on recipients in that context; administrative enforcement serves different aims and may lawfully impose different elements or thresholds. Courts have recognized the Department may use Davis/Gebser as a starting point and adapt the framework for administrative enforcement.
